summary: With an In and an Out set, you can play just the marked stretch: it starts at the In and stops on the Out. Plain Space still plays to the end.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walks: play-in-to-out-walk, play-in-to-out-from-the-ruler-walk.

try.do: Open a screen recording and click the timeline so it has the keyboard.
Put the playhead somewhere, press I; move it later, press O.
Watch it stop on the Out mark.
Press Space: it plays on past the Out, as before.
Right-click the ruler and choose Play In to Out.
Clear both marks (Option-X) and press Command-Shift-Space: nothing happens, and the Video menu row is dimmed.

evaluate: Is Command-Shift-Space a key your hand would find, given Premiere's Mac key (Option-K) is Previous Key here?
Does stopping exactly on the Out feel right, or would you rather it looped the stretch?
Is the ruler menu, beside Set In and Set Out, where you would look for it?
Should the transport carry a Play In to Out button, the way Premiere's monitor does?
rough: Premiere's Mac key for Play In to Out is Option-K, which Photonz already spends on Go to Previous Key, so this uses Premiere's Windows chord with Command for Control.
J, K or L pressed during a Play In to Out takes over and no longer stops at the Out.
No mock page shows this command, so there was nothing to compare side by side; it lives in the Video menu and the ruler's right-click menu.
